thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: GPU OOM spike in inference-prod-pool-2 (alerts: 18 nodes reporting OOM within 5m). Autoresolution window: 30m.

pagerduty: Incident #PD-78321 - severity: p1. Multiple CUDA OOM errors observed, error signature 'CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY' coming from model-serving pods (replica label=redwood-serving-v3).

sara: acked. I'm on it — switching pager to myself. Checking metrics + logs.

olivia: seeing p95 token latency jump from 120ms -> 900ms on hosted API. 503s increased ~12% over the last 4m. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/services/inference -> panel 'gpu_mem_pressure'.

raj: noted. Which model family? any throttling/batch changes?

sara: it looks like the majority of OOMs are from requests hitting long sequence lengths to redwood-large-70b on pool-2 (gpu type A100-80GB). KV cache growth + concurrent prefix batching seems to be hitting memory. some pods show the following in kube logs:

```
2026-03-14T18:12:03Z ERROR runtime: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY during forward
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/srv/serve/runner.py", line 412, in _step
    out = model.forward(inputs)
  File "/opt/runtime/kernel.cu", line 1287, in run
CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
```

matt: hmm. Autoscaler didn't spin new nodes? Cluster quota shows low remaining GPU capacity in us-east-1. Could be region quota exhaustion.

olivia: customer impact: high for several hosted customers — we have 7 active sessions showing repeated 5xxs, top reported customer is acme-search-prod (they're sending long-guided-doc queries).

raj: priority mitigation plan: 1) stop accepting new long-seq requests to redwood-large-70b on this pool (traffic cutoff), 2) route new traffic to fallback model variant (redwood-large-70b-q4_1 / or redwood-medium-7b) in other pools/regions, 3) restart affected pods after disabling continuous-batching temporarily, 4) scale up dedicated capacity if quota allows.

sara: executing step 1 now: applying runtime routing policy to reject new requests with seq_len>4096 for pool inference-prod-pool-2. Command: `redwoodctl routing apply --pool inference-prod-pool-2 --rule "max_seq_len:4096 -> reject"`

deploy-bot: routing policy applied (id=routing-2026-03-14-001). 0 failures.

matt: I'm toggling canary fallback to route 60% of new API traffic for those models to us-west-2 where we have spare GPUs. `redwoodctl route set --from-hosted --model redwood-large-70b --to region:us-west-2 --pct 60`

deploy-bot: route update accepted. Canary id=canary-1453.

olivia: reducing batch sizes for the serving runtime on the impacted pool might reduce pressure. Anyone want me to apply a temporary max_batch=1 override?

raj: yes, do it. Also disable prefix caching per request to avoid KV cache growth.

olivia: applying override: `kubectl -n inference set env ds/serve-runtime MAX_BATCH=1 PREFIX_CACHE_ENABLED=false --record`

incident-bot: Action logged by olivia.

sara: I'm restarting the worst offenders one-by-one (pods with >75% memory usage and OOM events). Doing rolling pod restart with 30s between restarts.

matt: checking quota requests to request more GPUs: filed AZ quota increase ticket to cloud: ticket #CLD-99244 (requesting +8 A100s in us-east-1). ETA ~20-40m.

raj: if cloud quota is slow, we should fallback more aggressively to redwood-medium or redirect heavy seq workloads to CPU-inference nodes temporarily. Costly but keeps customers online.

olivia: CPU fallback tested for small models. For 70b it's not feasible. I'm steering acme-search-prod to redwood-medium-7b as a temporary policy for their tenant id. `redwoodctl tenant route --tenant acme-search-prod --model redwood-medium-7b`

acme-search-prod (via webhook): we're seeing reduced latency after fallback but some result regressions, they accept degraded quality for availability. :thumbsup:

sara: observed immediate reduction in OOM rate after batch=1 + disabling prefix cache + routing cutoffs. OOM count dropped from 18 -> 3 in 6 minutes. p95 latency still elevated but trending down.

matt: good. I'm going to take over the pager in 10m when my shift starts — Sara, can you handoff after the next restart completes?

sara: yes. I'll summarize current state and handoff. Current: routing cutoff in place, canary routing 60% to us-west-2, batch override set, restarted 12 pods (3 remaining), cloud quota ticket open, acme-search routed to medium fallback. Next steps: finish restarts, monitor for OOMs 15m window, if still >5 OOMs escalate to infra.

matt: ack. I'll keep an eye on logs and dashboards. If OOMs continue, prepare to temporarily disable continuous KV caching globally on that pool.

olivia: posting relevant dashboards in thread: `grafana: /d/xYz/inference-prod` and logs link: `https://logs.redwood/svc=inference/err?query=CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY`.

deploy-bot: 3rd restart completed for pod serve-45c2; health checks passing.

sara: handing over: handoff note -> current mitigations in place, impact limited, acme-search on fallback, cloud ticket CLD-99244 pending. I'll update incident doc after 30m stability window. @matt take the pager.

matt: taking pager. Thanks @sara.

raj: leaving a quick nudge about postmortem: please record sequence length distribution for the last 72h and check whether prompt expansion (structured outputs) increased average seq by >15%. Action item: PR to enforce per-tenant seq-limits for heavy models.

sara: noted. I'll open the postmortem ticket after we confirm stable.

incident-bot: Auto-update: OOM events over last 10m: 2. p95 latency down to 310ms.

matt: after 25m of zero OOMs and stable p95 under 350ms, I'm going to mark this incident as mitigated and move to monitoring. Please add any follow-up tasks to PD-78321.

olivia: adding follow-up: (1) add per-tenant seq limit in runtime policy, (2) make autoscaler sensitive to rapid KV cache growth, (3) run canary load tests for long-seq workloads.

sara: I'll attach the logs and the list of restarted pods to PD-78321. Thanks team.

pagerduty: PD-78321 status changed: mitigated by sara, oncall transferred to matt.

matt: closing the thread for now. Will reopen if things regress.

incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigated). Follow-up tasks required.
